chapter: Stuff Smith stories, Wes Montgomery and singers
title: How the Stuff Smith Trio avoided the draft: Stuff's act and Jones's heart murmur
summary: Stuff drank water and vomited on the psychiatrist's desk, John Levy feigned craziness, and Jones was rejected for his heart murmur.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Last night at the meeting -- after the meeting of the Jazz Heritage Foundation board, you and Marl Marie Young were talking and one of the stories you were telling was about how the Stuff Smith Trio didn't get drafted and why, during World War II.
Oh, okay. Well, Stuff had -- well, he wasn't dangerously insane or anything like that, but he had just come out of -- Kankakee, Illinois, you know.
Uh-huh.
And he would go off sometimes, and I think women really triggered it.
Really?
(Laughter)

I think he was having a little trouble with his wife and he would go off on an oblique angle or something. And John Levy went -- he went into Nutsville, he put on an act. Everybody was finding something to do to stay out of the war, you know?
Well, didn't Marl Marie Young say that John Levy went down to the draft board and said that he was eager to be there, please put a gun in his hand --
So he could shoot every white cat in the back of the head.
That's right, he wants to go shoot white people, quick.

Yeah. So Stuff had another thing going, in that he could drink a lot of water and he could throw up, you know, anytime he wanted to. And when he got to the psychiatrist's desk, the guy was writing down, you know, answers, questions and answers, you know.
Uh-huh.
And Stuff threw up all over the man's desk.
On purpose.
Yeah. He waited. He drank the water and timed it just right.
(Laughter)

And so the guy put 4-F, he stamped 4-F all over his papers, you know, and put him out of the building. And I was lucky in another way, in that I've always had a heart murmur. Still have it, you know, had it all my life. I think it's genetic, because my parents, you know, both of them were cardio-vascular victims, and so they took me back, they had like special rooms. You know, you go through the whole examination, then they would send you back to a specialist in the building.
Uh-huh.
So they sent me back to the heart specialist, and they rejected me, you know.
Which kept the trio intact.
Yes. We all went right back to work.
(Laughter)
But that thing with Stuff Smith and Petrillo was -- that's a classic story.
